doc: surface_contrasts(img, land, deck): area-weighted (cos lat, float64) means of the map over masks with |lat| < 60: land (land > 0.5, strict, in the dtype of land), ocean, 15..35 degree land and ocean, north, south, 40..60 north and south, the ocean-only north-minus-south pairs, the differences, and itcz_lat = the mean latitude of the 2.5-degree zonal-mean bands (|lat| < 20) whose mean is >= max - 0.02; with a deck: ocean 8..35 degrees under a deck (deck > 0.3) and with none (deck < 0.05), both strict, compared in the deck's own dtype (a float32 deck against 0.3 compares float32(0.3): a texel equal to it is NOT under a deck). A mask with no texel gives 0 (the 1e-12 floor). The values come back in the order of params.keys. Maps are stored u8 and divided by 255 in float32 (land and deck as Surface.load does) unless the doc says otherwise. A 64x32 float32 map: rows are 5.6 degrees apart, so some 2.5-degree bands inside 20 degrees hold no row and are NaN; ps.max() is then NaN (numpy propagates it), no band passes the comparison and itcz_lat is the mean of an empty set = NaN. Every other value is finite. Rust f64::max ignores NaN: do not port the max with it. Float64 formula on float32 or float64 inputs, summed by numpy (pairwise): against exactly rounded sums it differs by 2.7e-16 relative, so 1e-9. The itcz_lat crest picks bands by a hard threshold on float32 row means; params.itcz_threshold_margin is the smallest gap between a 2.5-degree band mean and the max - 0.02 threshold, > 1e-5 (a float32 rounding is 1e-7), so the selection is stable.
